# LDAP search filter built from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/ldap-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-90](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/90.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in the text of an LDAP search filter (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta REST):
the filter of JNDI `DirContext.search`, the `String` filter of Spring LDAP's `LdapTemplate`
methods, and hand-written filters given to `LdapQueryBuilder.filter(...)`. Filter arguments
(`{0}`), Spring LDAP's query builder and filter classes, and encoded values are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Characters such as `*`, `(`, `)` and `\` have a meaning in a filter. A user name of `*` matches
every entry, and `admin)(|(uid=*` rewrites the filter. Depending on the query, that can bypass a
login check, reveal other users' data, or make the directory return far more than intended.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the uid is concatenated into the filter.

```java
package com.example.directory;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import javax.naming.NamingEnumeration;
import javax.naming.NamingException;
import javax.naming.directory.DirContext;
import javax.naming.directory.SearchControls;
import javax.naming.directory.SearchResult;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class UserController {
    private DirContext ctx;

    @GetMapping("/users")
    public List<String> find(@RequestParam String uid) throws NamingException {
        NamingEnumeration<SearchResult> results =
                ctx.search("ou=people,dc=example,dc=com", "(uid=" + uid + ")", new SearchControls());
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        while (results.hasMore()) {
            names.add(results.next().getNameInNamespace());
        }
        return names;
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the uid is a filter argument, which JNDI escapes.

```java
package com.example.directory;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import javax.naming.NamingEnumeration;
import javax.naming.NamingException;
import javax.naming.directory.DirContext;
import javax.naming.directory.SearchControls;
import javax.naming.directory.SearchResult;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class UserController {
    private DirContext ctx;

    @GetMapping("/users")
    public List<String> find(@RequestParam String uid) throws NamingException {
        NamingEnumeration<SearchResult> results = ctx.search(
                "ou=people,dc=example,dc=com", "(uid={0})", new Object[] {uid}, new SearchControls());
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        while (results.hasMore()) {
            names.add(results.next().getNameInNamespace());
        }
        return names;
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Pass the value as a filter argument: JNDI
  `search(name, "(uid={0})", new Object[] { value }, controls)`, Spring LDAP
  `query().where("uid").is(value)` or `filter("(uid={0})", value)`, or a filter class such as
  `EqualsFilter`.
- Or escape it for a filter: Spring LDAP `LdapEncoder.filterEncode(value)` or ESAPI
  `encodeForLDAP(value)`.
- Distinguished names need their own escaping (`LdapEncoder.nameEncode`, `LdapNameBuilder`).
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)
- JNDI (javax.naming.directory)
- Spring LDAP

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Only the search filter is checked: a distinguished name built from request data (the search
  base, a lookup or bind name) is not reported, although it needs DN escaping.
- Spring LDAP filter classes (`EqualsFilter`, `LikeFilter`, ...) count as encoding their value only
  when the attribute name is a literal; `LikeFilter` keeps `*` as a wildcard by design.
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), except a Spring `HttpEntity` or `RequestEntity` (the
  request body and headers); enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as request data.
- One method is analysed at a time and conditions are not evaluated. Allow-list lookups are
  recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants and as `valueOf` of an enum declared in the same
  file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

The test file [`rules/java/ldap/ldap-injection.java`](../../../rules/java/ldap/ldap-injection.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
